issues.title: Doc claims reading source to an exception always closes it; one path doesn't
issues.verdictReason: source_impl::operator() (include/seastar/rpc/rpc_impl.hh:941-982) only calls close_source() on the smp::submit_to/stream_receive path (eof or failure); when _bufs is non-empty it returns process_one_buffer() directly, so an exception thrown by unmarshall() there propagates without ever calling close_source(), leaving _source_closed false.
issues.scopeReason: The 'Closing a stream' section and its absolute claim about throwing are new text added by this PR (doc/rpc-streaming.md).

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The docs say that reading the source until it throws closes it. That is not true for every exception the source can throw.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The docs say that reading the source until it throws closes it. That is not true for every exception the source can throw.

issues.title: Doc/commit overstate that the stream connection only shuts down once both halves close
issues.verdictReason: client::loop() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:1012-1077) tears the connection down (stop_send_loop, _outstanding.clear(), _stopped.set_value()) whenever the receive loop hits eof or _error, independent of stream_check_twoway_closed(); client::abort_all_streams() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:848-855) can set that _error via abort() without either half being app-closed, so the connection can fully stop without both halves being closed, contradicting the absolute wording in both the doc and the commit message.
issues.scopeReason: Both the doc sentence and the commit message making this claim are new, added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new docs say the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed, and commit 3 says closing one half means it is never shut down. Both are false.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The new docs say the stream's connection is shut down only once both halves are closed, and commit 3 says closing one half means it is never shut down. Both are false.

issues.title: stream_close() comment wrongly claims only the trailing stop() sets _error
issues.verdictReason: handle_stream_frame() sets _error = true directly on an eof-like read result (src/rpc/rpc.cc:588), and client::loop()'s receive path (src/rpc/rpc.cc:1020/1065) also sets it; these can run concurrently with stream_close() on the same connection, so _error is not 'only set by the stop() that follows'.
issues.scopeReason: The comment is new, added by this PR's stream_close() change.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The new stream_close() comment says _error is only set by the stop() that follows, but several other paths set _error concurrently.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The new stream_close() comment says _error is only set by the stop() that follows, but several other paths set _error concurrently.

issues.title: Regression test can hang: untimed cv wait and release only reached on success path
issues.verdictReason: st.close_entered_cv.wait(...) has no timeout, and st.release_close.set_value() is only reached after the unguarded stream_send_empty_frame().get() call and sink_closed.get()/server_done.get(); any exception other than rpc::closed_error thrown there propagates out of the lambda before release_close is ever set, permanently parking test_data_sink_impl::close() (and the test).
issues.scopeReason: This is new test code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The test waits on close_entered_cv without a timeout, and it releases close only on the success path. Any exception between sink.close() and set_value() leaves the write-buffer close parked forever.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The test waits on close_entered_cv without a timeout, and it releases close only on the success path. Any exception between sink.close() and set_value() leaves the write-buffer close parked forever.

issues.title: New regression test never exercises the outgoing-queue-drain half of the fix
issues.verdictReason: By the time the test observes close_entered (src/rpc/rpc.cc stream_close() already set _stream_closing and already invoked write_buf.close()), _stream_closing alone is enough for send() to reject the hook's frame (src/rpc/rpc.cc:293); a fix that added only the _stream_closing flag, without the new queue_drained wait before write_buf.close(), would still make this test pass, so the queue-drain behavior itself is untested.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new, added by this PR to cover its own fix.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The regression test does not cover the second half of the fix, which waits for `_outgoing_queue` to drain before closing. A fix that only sets `_stream_closing` would pass the test.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The regression test does not cover the second half of the fix, which waits for `_outgoing_queue` to drain before closing. A fix that only sets `_stream_closing` would pass the test.

issues.title: Test doesn't assert the stated closed_error contract, only the absence of a late write
issues.verdictReason: The try/catch around stream_send_empty_frame().get() silently accepts a non-throwing result, and the only BOOST_REQUIRE in the test checks st.put_after_close; the commit's stated contract ('send() refuses with closed_error once stream_close() has begun') is never asserted directly.
issues.scopeReason: The test is new, added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The test accepts the hook returning success as well as closed_error, and only asserts on put_after_close. It never checks the PR's stated contract that send() is refused with closed_error once stream_close() has begun.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The test accepts the hook returning success as well as closed_error, and only asserts on put_after_close. It never checks the PR's stated contract that send() is refused with closed_error once stream_close() has begun.

issues.title: stream_close() now waits unboundedly for the whole outgoing queue to drain
issues.verdictReason: Before this PR, stream_close() called write_buf.close() immediately; now it first awaits queue_drained (the whole chained _outgoing_queue_ready, not just the in-flight entry as stop_send_loop's withdraw() does at src/rpc/rpc.cc:206-221), and send_entry()'s write_buf.flush() (src/rpc/rpc.cc:186-189) has no timeout, so a stalled socket with queued stream entries can block sink.close() (and thus stream_close()/stop()) indefinitely.
issues.scopeReason: This waiting behavior is newly introduced by this PR's stream_close() change.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: stream_close() now waits for the whole outgoing queue to drain before closing the write buffer, and nothing bounds or cancels this wait.

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: stream_close() now waits for the whole outgoing queue to drain before closing the write buffer, and nothing bounds or cancels this wait.

issues.title: Test data_sink wrapper's put() override isn't API-level guarded like the base it copies
issues.verdictReason: include/seastar/core/iostream.hh:104-128 declares put(std::span<...>) as pure virtual only when SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9, and put(net::packet) as the pure virtual otherwise; tests/unit/loopback_socket.hh:144-153 mirrors this with an #if/#else providing the matching override for either level, but the PR's new test_data_sink_impl::put(std::span<temporary_buffer<char>>) override (tests/unit/rpc_test.cc ~1883) is unconditional, so building with Seastar_API_LEVEL=7 or 8 (still a supported CMake option) leaves data_sink_impl::put(net::packet) unimplemented and the class fails to compile/instantiate.
issues.scopeReason: test_data_sink_impl is new code added by this PR.

reportedAs.review-and-fix-pr: The test's data_sink wrapper overrides only put(std::span<...>), with no SEASTAR_API_LEVEL guard. The loopback sink it wraps guards that overload with #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 and also implements put(net::packet).

reportedAsByRun.rafp-added-diff-2026-10-09/ironweave/rev: The test's data_sink wrapper overrides only put(std::span<...>), with no SEASTAR_API_LEVEL guard. The loopback sink it wraps guards that overload with #if SEASTAR_API_LEVEL >= 9 and also implements put(net::packet).
